::: {.callout-note}
## TL;DR

- `git clone <url>#<branch>` is **not** Git syntax. It is the npm-style dependency notation. Pass the branch with `-b` (`--branch`)
- Add `--single-branch` to fetch only that branch's history, and `--depth 1` to fetch only its latest commit
- Already cloned? Just `git switch <branch>`

:::{.code-area}

```zsh
# check out release/1.0 right after cloning
git clone -b release/1.0 https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git

# fetch only release/1.0
git clone -b release/1.0 --single-branch https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git

# fetch only the latest commit of release/1.0
git clone -b release/1.0 --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git

# already cloned
git switch release/1.0
```

:::

:::


## 🎯 Goal

- [ ] Clone a repository with a specific branch checked out
- [ ] Choose between a full, single-branch, and shallow clone


## 🔎 Objective

You want the `release/1.0` branch of `sample-app`, not the default branch. Writing the
branch after a `#`, the way `package.json` does, looks natural:

:::{.code-area}

```zsh
# ❌ does not select a branch
git clone https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git#release/1.0
```

:::

- `npm install github:example-org/sample-app#release/1.0` understands `#<branch>`, but `git clone`
does not. 
- Git has no branch part in its URL syntax, so `#release/1.0` is just part of the URL


## Solution: using `git clone -b`


::: {.callout-note}
### Check out a specific branch

:::{.code-area}

```zsh
git clone -b release/1.0 https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git
```

:::

This is a normal clone. Git fetches every branch, as usual, but checks out `release/1.0`
instead of the remote's default branch.


:::


:::: {.no-border-top-table}

| Option | Meaning |
| ------ | ------- |
| `-b <name>`, `--branch <name>` | Check out `<name>` instead of the branch the remote's `HEAD` points to. `<name>` can also be a tag; you then get a detached `HEAD` at that tag |
: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

::::

[Fetch only that branch]{.mini-section}

:::{.code-area}

```zsh
git clone -b release/1.0 --single-branch https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git
```

:::

`--single-branch` fetches only the history reachable from `release/1.0`, and sets the
remote's fetch refspec so that later `git fetch` runs also track only that branch.

[Fetch only the latest commit]{.mini-section}

:::{.code-area}

```zsh
git clone -b release/1.0 --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/example-org/sample-app.git
```

:::

`--depth 1` cuts the history down to the tip commit. Use this when you need the files but not
the history, e.g. in CI or to try out a build. It is the fastest option for large repositories.

:::: {.no-border-top-table}

| Option | Meaning |
| ------ | ------- |
| `--single-branch` | Fetch only the branch given by `-b` (or the remote's default branch when `-b` is omitted). Later `git fetch` runs track only that branch |
| `--depth <n>` | Create a shallow clone with only the last `<n>` commits. Implies `--single-branch` unless you pass `--no-single-branch` |
| `--no-single-branch` | Fetch the tips of all branches, even with `--depth` |
: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

::::

Since `--depth` already implies `--single-branch`, writing both is redundant, but harmless.
Keeping `--single-branch` in the command makes the intent explicit.

[Which one to use]{.mini-section}

:::: {.no-border-top-table}

| Command | Branches fetched | History fetched | Use when |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- | -------- |
| `git clone -b <branch>` | All | Full | You work on this branch but may switch to others |
| `git clone -b <branch> --single-branch` | `<branch>` only | Full | You only care about this branch, but need its log, `blame`, etc. |
| `git clone -b <branch> --depth 1` | `<branch>` only | Latest commit | You only need the files (CI, a quick build) |
: {tbl-colwidths="[34,16,16,34]"}

::::
